text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as a reading that is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg according to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

snippet_highlighted_words: a reading that is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg

text_blocks.snippet: Readings are measured in millimeters of mercury (mm Hg) and split into top (systolic) and bottom (diastolic) numbers:

list.snippet: Elevated: 120–129 systolic and less than 80 diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
Hypertensive Crisis (Emergency): Higher than 180 and/or 120 mm Hg (Seek emergency care immediately if accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, numbness, or weakness)
